findingDetails.title: The dependency object env does not reach the receipt path, so a caller that injects only env still writes to and reads from the real temporary folder
findingDetails.claim: buildAdvisorPart accepts env for deterministic tests, but headReceiptDir and the default read and write keep using process.env and tmpdir(), so env only changes the child-session test.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the suite; it injects read and write, so the default path is untested and the gap is in the documented dependency surface.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The env dependency could be scoped to child detection only; the object is documented as one injectable bundle, so a caller cannot tell.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: None; the default path is reachable by any caller that injects only env.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The part and its suite are declared scope files; read, write and env are accepted in the same documented dependency object.

findingDetails.title: The doctor contract test name says it checks DSH only while it now asserts the Vibe rows too
findingDetails.claim: MIRROR_CHECKS is the union of DSH and Vibe rows and routeGaps iterates both, but the route test is still named for the three DSH checks.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the union and both gap walks; the coverage is complete and only the title is stale.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The name could be read as a historical label; it is the string CI prints, so it misattributes a Vibe failure.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: None; the changed array makes the title false.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The contract test is a declared scope file and the changed line added the Vibe rows to the same array.
